name: HUD Fair Market Rents (FMR)
what_it_measures: Annual estimate of gross rent (rent + utilities) at the 40th percentile of the local rental market, by unit size (efficiency through 4BR), for every county/CBSA/ZIP-area in the US. Published by HUD PD&R; used nationally to set Section 8 payment standards.
coverage: national (all US counties, CBSAs, and HUD-defined metro FMR areas)
granularity: county / CBSA (also has a 'Small Area FMR' variant at ZIP-code level for ~80 designated metro areas)
history_available: Static annual schedules published back to the 1980s on huduser.gov; the documented API (per third-party wrappers like the R packages hudr/rhud) exposes current and some recent prior fiscal years by county FIPS or CBSA code — exact API history depth not independently confirmed, see caveats.
access_method: Free HUD FMR API (token via huduser.gov registration), with a state endpoint (all counties/metros in a state) and an entity endpoint (by county FIPS or CBSA code). Also plain CSV/Excel bulk downloads per fiscal year on huduser.gov if the API's range turns out to be thin.
license: Listed as Public Domain by a third-party API aggregator (apis.io), linking to HUD's own API ToS. Not independently verified against HUD's ToS page in this run.
cost: free (requires a free API token, no payment, no trial window)
rate_limit: not confirmed in this run; typical of federal statistical APIs (generous, no paid tier)
fills_gap: Rent-side input for investment yield/cash-flow estimates (scoring/investment.py) and for the neighborhood growth score's rent signal, in any county nationwide. zillow_research.py's ZHVI/ZORI pull is itself national data but is filtered down to NYC's 5 counties (NYC_COUNTIES) in the adapter as written, and RentCast listings are budget-capped at 31 requests/month. census_acs.py is also national-grade ACS data in principle, but as implemented it's hardcoded to NYC's 5 counties (COUNTIES = NY/Kings/Queens/Bronx/Richmond, state:36 only) and its VARS list has no rent variable (no B25064-type field) at all. So today there is no rent benchmark anywhere outside NYC in this codebase; FMR would be the first one.
caveats: Need to confirm exactly how many fiscal years the live API exposes vs. requiring a scrape of static per-year CSV/Excel schedules for a backtest-length history.

FMR is a regulatory rent-setting number (40th percentile), not a transaction-based market rent index — treat as a rent *level* benchmark, not a rent *growth* signal; pair with Zillow ZORI (where available) for trend.
License should be re-confirmed directly on huduser.gov/HUD's API ToS page (not just a third-party aggregator) before an add-data-source implementation.

Census ACS table B25064 (median gross rent, tract-level, national) is a free alternative/complement already inside the project's existing Census API key and billing — worth a look before assuming FMR is the only option, though it would need census_acs.py's county allowlist and VARS extended, which it doesn't do today.
recommendation_note: Free, public-domain-licensed, genuinely national at county granularity, no API-budget conflict with RentCast. Directly fills a real, stated gap (rent benchmark outside NYC) rather than duplicating an existing source. Confirm the live API's historical depth and re-check the official ToS page during add-data-source implementation, but nothing found in this search raises a cost or license blocker.
